gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 27?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 27 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated guidance ahead of resolution will refine these short-range projections.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models from sources including DWD, ECMWF, and GFS indicate a high near 28–29°C in Munich on August 28, 2026, driven by warm southeasterly advection on the 27th followed by a shift to northwesterly flow and increasing convective instability.** Afternoon thunderstorms, with probabilities exceeding 60% in several runs, are expected to develop as daytime heating peaks, potentially limiting the maximum through evaporative cooling and cloud cover or allowing brief spikes if convection is delayed. This keeps 28°C and 29°C as the closest outcomes in trader sentiment, while a 30°C+ result would require stronger insolation and suppressed precipitation than current ensemble guidance suggests. Above the long-term average high of roughly 23°C, the setup reflects typical late-summer pattern variability rather than an extreme heat episode. Updated model runs over the next 24–48 hours will refine timing of any convective initiation and thus the precise peak temperature.

**Persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and thunderstorms from an active frontal system are keeping daytime heating limited across the Kanto region, positioning 30°C as the clear market favorite for Tokyo’s August 27 high.** Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and multiple forecast models converge on a maximum near 30–32°C under mostly overcast skies, with precipitation probabilities around 50% through the afternoon. High humidity and light variable winds further suppress temperature rise by reducing solar insolation and enhancing evaporative cooling.

Recent observations show the same pattern holding through August 26, with highs in the low 30s amid frequent rain, and no signs of clearing that would allow stronger heating. While isolated model runs briefly suggest a brief 33°C spike if breaks in cloud cover occur, the weight of consensus and ongoing moisture advection keeps probabilities for 32°C and above low. The market’s heavy weighting toward 30°C (64%) reflects traders’ assessment that the current synoptic regime will persist through the resolution window, consistent with climatological late-August norms when disturbed weather dominates.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts from multiple models indicate a peak temperature in Munich on August 28 most likely between 28–30°C, driven by warm southeasterly flow ahead of an approaching frontal system, with trader odds reflecting this narrow band amid afternoon thunderstorm risk. Scattered convection, expected after midday per consensus runs, could limit surface heating through cloud cover and evaporative cooling, introducing uncertainty around whether the daily maximum occurs before or is suppressed by storms. Above-average conditions relative to the 1991–2020 August mean high of ~23°C increase the chance of 29–30°C outcomes if instability develops later, while earlier or stronger activity favors 28°C or below. Official updates from the German Weather Service and ECMWF ensemble members on timing and intensity remain the key variables for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Met Office forecasts and ensemble model runs position a 24–25°C peak as the most probable outcome for London on August 27, reflecting persistent cloud cover, light rain, and a moderating Atlantic airstream that limits solar heating. Traders appear to weigh these official guidance updates—showing maxima of 24–26°C with modest warming potential—more heavily than any outlier warmer scenarios, while very low odds on extremes above 27°C or below 23°C align with the narrow uncertainty range in current observational trends and short-range model consensus.

Trader emphasis on 24–25°C outcomes reflects these stabilizing influences and potential for localized cooling from rainfall, with 26°C remaining viable if clearing occurs earlier than expected.

Traders weigh the risk of lingering cloud or renewed showers against any late intensification, keeping 25 °C as the modal implied probability while assigning limited weight to extremes above 27 °C. Updated Met Office briefings through the afternoon will provide the next resolution-relevant data.

Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and multiple numerical models project a daytime maximum near 30–31°C under mostly cloudy skies with scattered showers or thunderstorms, which limit surface heating through reduced insolation and evaporative cooling. Recent days have featured highs of 32–35°C amid clearer conditions, but increased moisture and cloud cover on the 27th have moderated the peak. Historical late-August climatology for Tokyo (normal high ~30–31°C) aligns with this range, and live station data show temperatures tracking close to forecast guidance without significant upward surprises.

The 2.3% probability on 31°C and lower odds on other outcomes acknowledge minor forecast uncertainty from model spread on shower timing and intensity. A realistic challenge to the 30°C outcome would require either unexpectedly rapid clearing of clouds (allowing stronger solar heating) or a shift in steering patterns that reduces precipitation coverage. Conversely, heavier or more persistent rain could cap the high below 30°C, though current guidance does not support that scenario. Resolution will depend on the official Tokyo observation from the Japan Meteorological Agency.

Ensemble guidance shows limited spread, though modest variations in cloud cover or timing of any precipitation could shift the daily peak by 1–2°C. Trader positioning, with 25°C at 40.5% implied probability followed by 24°C and 23°C, mirrors this model consensus while acknowledging residual uncertainty ahead of final observational data.

**Trader sentiment for NYC's highest temperature on August 27, 2026, centers on 82-83°F as the leading outcome (48.5% implied probability), followed by 80-81°F (24%), reflecting consensus from National Weather Service and other models projecting a high in the lower-to-mid 80s amid unsettled conditions.**

Key drivers include widespread afternoon showers and thunderstorms (70% chance), which limit solar insolation and cap daytime peaks despite southerly flow and high humidity. Morning lows near 70-72°F and partly sunny starts give way to increasing cloud cover and convective activity by midday, with south winds of 10-15 mph (gusts to 25 mph) providing modest mixing but not enough to overcome the cooling effect of precipitation. This aligns with climatological norms for late August (average high ~82°F) but tilts cooler than clear-sky potential due to the frontal boundary and moisture.

Recent observations show stable early-morning readings around 72°F with no heat buildup, supporting the narrow range favored by markets. Higher outcomes (84°F+) carry lower odds as models show limited deviation from storm-suppressed maxima, while sub-80°F scenarios remain unlikely without stronger cooling. Updated forecasts and real-time observations through the afternoon will be the main near-term catalysts.

Official Met Office guidance points to a maximum near 26–27 °C once skies partially break, yet lingering cloud, showers, and modest southerly winds are limiting solar insolation and surface warming. Ensemble model spreads and recent observations show afternoon temperatures clustering between 24–25 °C in many runs, creating the tight market split between those two outcomes. Resolution hinges on the precise timing of rain clearance and any urban heat-island boost, with updated forecasts through the afternoon likely to refine the final hourly maximum recorded at official stations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Met Office and other agencies indicate a maximum of 23–24°C in London on August 28, supported by southwesterly flow advecting milder Atlantic air after Thursday’s thunderstorms. Partly cloudy skies with moderate winds of 10–15 mph will promote mixing and limit peak insolation, keeping daytime highs near the seasonal norm while suppressing stronger surface heating. Trader consensus clusters on 23°C and 24°C because ensemble guidance shows tight agreement on these values, with the 14% probability for 25°C or higher reflecting residual uncertainty in cloud timing and any localized clearing. New model runs and observational updates overnight will refine whether subtle shifts in wind direction or moisture alter the exact peak.

NWS point forecasts for Central Park and area airports explicitly call for a high near 83°F under partly sunny skies transitioning to mostly cloudy with storms, while neighboring guidance converges on 82°F. 

This setup explains the market’s secondary weighting toward 80–81°F (27.5%) and the lower odds on 84–85°F (12.5%), as convection and moisture limit upside. Historical analogs show similar late-August days rarely exceed the low-to-mid 80s without a strong ridge, and no such anomalous pattern is present. With the day underway and resolution based on official observations (likely shifting to The Weather Company data), traders are heavily weighting the consensus forecast range.

Traders weigh these variables against hourly model updates expected overnight, reflecting genuine forecast divergence rather than a narrow consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts indicate persistent cloud cover and scattered showers across Tokyo on August 29, limiting daytime heating and supporting peak temperatures near 27–28°C. Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency highlights cloudy conditions with occasional rain, consistent with multiple global models showing suppressed maxima relative to the late-August climatological average of around 30–31°C. Variable steering patterns and precipitation timing create the narrow spread in market-implied odds, as even modest shifts in cloud breaks or rainfall intensity can alter the daily high by 1–2°C. Traders appear to weigh the strong consensus for a cooler, unsettled day against residual uncertainty in short-range model solutions ahead of final observational data.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus on the Polymarket heavily favors a London maximum temperature of 24°C or 25°C on August 27, 2026 (combined ~74% implied probability), reflecting the latest Met Office and numerical guidance showing a warm but rain-suppressed day.**

A humid air mass with temperatures in the low-to-mid 20s has been offset by widespread cloud cover, heavy morning rain, and thunderstorms across southeast England. Official forecasts highlight a maximum of 26–27°C under clearer spells, yet persistent precipitation and reduced insolation have kept surface readings closer to 23–25°C through midday observations at Heathrow and other stations. Model consensus from GFS and UKMO runs points to afternoon highs around 24–25°C once rain clears northward, with steering winds and modest instability limiting further warming.

Recent developments include active yellow thunderstorm warnings and flood alerts, which have reinforced expectations of limited solar heating. Historical late-August baselines for London (around 22–24°C) provide context, but today’s convective regime and high dew points favor the market’s leading outcomes over higher or lower extremes. Updated model runs and official briefings through the afternoon will remain key for any late shifts.

Ensemble guidance shows modest spread in peak values due to uncertainty in cloud breaks and shower timing, supporting the closely matched market-implied odds between 23°C and 24°C while capping upside risk for 25°C or higher. Historical late-August baselines around 21–22°C provide context for the slightly above-average outlook under current synoptic conditions. Traders will watch the next high-resolution model runs and morning Met Office briefing for any shifts in the expected maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwesterly flow and widespread cloud cover associated with an unsettled Atlantic low-pressure system are capping insolation and advecting cooler maritime air across southeast England, keeping forecast maximums tightly clustered around 20–22 °C for 29 August. Official guidance from the Met Office and ensemble output place the daytime peak near 22 °C under mostly overcast skies with periods of rain, while some guidance shows slightly lower values near 18–20 °C if heavier showers persist through the afternoon. The narrow spread in market-implied probabilities (21 °C at 27 %, 22 °C at 25 %, 20 °C at 18.5 %) reflects modest ensemble divergence in cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing rather than any large-scale regime shift. Updated model runs and surface observations over the next 48 hours will determine whether brief breaks allow temperatures to reach the upper end of the distribution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwesterly flow and widespread cloud cover associated with an unsettled Atlantic low-pressure system are capping insolation and advecting cooler maritime air across southeast England, keeping forecast maximums tightly clustered around 20–22 °C for 29 August. Official guidance from the Met Office and ensemble output place the daytime peak near 22 °C under mostly overcast skies with periods of rain, while some guidance shows slightly lower values near 18–20 °C if heavier showers persist through the afternoon. The narrow spread in market-implied probabilities (21 °C at 27 %, 22 °C at 25 %, 20 °C at 18.5 %) reflects modest ensemble divergence in cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing rather than any large-scale regime shift. Updated model runs and surface observations over the next 48 hours will determine whether brief breaks allow temperatures to reach the upper end of the distribution.

The primary drivers are an unsettled post-frontal regime: a southwesterly flow advecting milder but not exceptionally warm Atlantic air, combined with variable cloud cover and showers that limit surface heating. Afternoon temperatures typically peak between 13:00–16:00 BST; breaks in cloud could allow brief warming toward 24°C, while persistent showers or thicker stratiform cloud would cap readings closer to 22–23°C. Recent thundery activity on the 27th has left residual moisture and a relatively cool boundary layer that further moderates the following day’s peak.

Model consensus remains tight but carries typical late-summer uncertainty from shower timing and exact cloud fraction. Historical late-August maxima in London average around 21–22°C, so the current setup sits slightly above normal yet well below heatwave thresholds. With 24°C edging 23°C in the market, traders are pricing in a modest chance of a few tenths of a degree extra insolation versus the risk of heavier or earlier rain suppressing the peak. New model runs and updated Met Office forecasts over the next 12–18 hours will be the key catalysts for any shift.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and northeasterly flow are the dominant factors capping Tokyo’s maximum temperature on August 29 near 27–29 °C.** Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models shows a moist airmass and frontal influence maintaining widespread stratiform clouds and periodic light rain through the day. These conditions sharply reduce incoming solar radiation, limiting surface heating compared with the climatological late-August average of ~31 °C.

Northeast winds of 5–10 m s⁻¹ advect cooler, more stable marine air while elevated humidity (often >80 %) further suppresses the diurnal temperature range. Forecast soundings indicate a shallow mixed layer and modest CAPE, so any convective cells are expected to be short-lived and inefficient at clearing cloud decks. Consequently, the daily maximum is likely to occur only briefly in the early afternoon before renewed showers or thickening cloud arrives.

Market-implied probabilities cluster tightly around 27–28 °C because ensemble members and high-resolution guidance differ mainly on the exact timing and coverage of the showers rather than on large-scale thermal advection. A modest break in cloud or delayed rain could briefly push readings to 29 °C, while steadier precipitation or thicker low-level stratus would favor 27 °C or lower. Updated JMA and global model runs issued in the next 24–36 hours will be the key catalysts for any shift in trader positioning ahead of the 29 August observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and northeasterly flow are the dominant factors capping Tokyo’s maximum temperature on August 29 near 27–29 °C.** Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models shows a moist airmass and frontal influence maintaining widespread stratiform clouds and periodic light rain through the day. These conditions sharply reduce incoming solar radiation, limiting surface heating compared with the climatological late-August average of ~31 °C.

Northeast winds of 5–10 m s⁻¹ advect cooler, more stable marine air while elevated humidity (often >80 %) further suppresses the diurnal temperature range. Forecast soundings indicate a shallow mixed layer and modest CAPE, so any convective cells are expected to be short-lived and inefficient at clearing cloud decks. Consequently, the daily maximum is likely to occur only briefly in the early afternoon before renewed showers or thickening cloud arrives.

Market-implied probabilities cluster tightly around 27–28 °C because ensemble members and high-resolution guidance differ mainly on the exact timing and coverage of the showers rather than on large-scale thermal advection. A modest break in cloud or delayed rain could briefly push readings to 29 °C, while steadier precipitation or thicker low-level stratus would favor 27 °C or lower. Updated JMA and global model runs issued in the next 24–36 hours will be the key catalysts for any shift in trader positioning ahead of the 29 August observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and model consensus indicate a partly sunny Friday in New York City with afternoon showers or thunderstorms possible, supporting highs centered in the low-to-mid 80s. West-to-northwest winds around 5 mph and increasing cloud cover from daytime heating limit surface warming, while dew points near 70°F add humidity that favors scattered convection rather than widespread heat buildup. These conditions align with the market’s leading probabilities on 82–83°F, followed closely by the 80–81°F and 84–85°F bins, as traders weigh typical late-August variability and the modest risk of brief clearing that could push readings a degree or two higher. Updated model runs and the 6 p.m. NWS forecast will provide the next key data points before settlement.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts indicate a high near 23–24°C for Munich on August 29, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s top probabilities (25°C at 39.5%, 24°C at 29.5%, 26°C at 15.5%).** Multiple models, including outputs reflected in sources such as globalmeteo, WeatherBug, weather-atlas, and Yr.no, converge on this range after warmer conditions earlier in the week.

A weather system bringing increased cloud cover, westerly flow, and scattered showers or thunderstorms—particularly evident on August 28—will suppress daytime heating on the 29th. This produces a cooler profile than the seasonal average high of ~22.8°C and far below recent peaks near 29–32°C. Afternoon clearing in some runs allows temperatures to reach the low-to-mid 20s°C, while any lingering rain or thicker cloud would cap the maximum lower.

Traders appear to weight the model consensus heavily, with limited dispersion around 24–25°C reflecting typical forecast uncertainty in maximum temperature two days out. Minor shifts in the timing of frontal passage or precipitation could still nudge the observed high by 1–2°C, but current guidance supports the clustered probabilities rather than outliers above 27°C or below 22°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Strong seasonal climatology and current forecast consensus from agencies like the Japan Meteorological Agency and international models underpin the near-certain market-implied odds for a Tokyo high reaching or exceeding 30°C on August 27.** Late August typically features average daily highs of 31–32°C in Tokyo, driven by persistent subtropical high pressure, warm sea-surface temperatures, and southerly flow. Real-time observations and model runs show daytime temperatures climbing to 30–32°C amid partly cloudy to mostly cloudy conditions with possible scattered showers, consistent with historical patterns where August maxima routinely surpass this threshold. Minor variability from localized convection or timing of any rain could affect the precise peak reading by a degree or two, yet conditions would need an improbable sharp cooling intrusion to keep the high below 30°C.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts indicate a high near 23–24°C for Munich on August 29, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s top probabilities (25°C at 39.5%, 24°C at 29.5%, 26°C at 15.5%).** Multiple models, including outputs reflected in sources such as globalmeteo, WeatherBug, weather-atlas, and Yr.no, converge on this range after warmer conditions earlier in the week.

A weather system bringing increased cloud cover, westerly flow, and scattered showers or thunderstorms—particularly evident on August 28—will suppress daytime heating on the 29th. This produces a cooler profile than the seasonal average high of ~22.8°C and far below recent peaks near 29–32°C. Afternoon clearing in some runs allows temperatures to reach the low-to-mid 20s°C, while any lingering rain or thicker cloud would cap the maximum lower.

Traders appear to weight the model consensus heavily, with limited dispersion around 24–25°C reflecting typical forecast uncertainty in maximum temperature two days out. Minor shifts in the timing of frontal passage or precipitation could still nudge the observed high by 1–2°C, but current guidance supports the clustered probabilities rather than outliers above 27°C or below 22°C.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts indicate a high near 23–24°C for Munich on August 29, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s top probabilities (25°C at 39.5%, 24°C at 29.5%, 26°C at 15.5%).** Multiple models, including outputs reflected in sources such as globalmeteo, WeatherBug, weather-atlas, and Yr.no, converge on this range after warmer conditions earlier in the week.

A weather system bringing increased cloud cover, westerly flow, and scattered showers or thunderstorms—particularly evident on August 28—will suppress daytime heating on the 29th. This produces a cooler profile than the seasonal average high of ~22.8°C and far below recent peaks near 29–32°C. Afternoon clearing in some runs allows temperatures to reach the low-to-mid 20s°C, while any lingering rain or thicker cloud would cap the maximum lower.

Traders appear to weight the model consensus heavily, with limited dispersion around 24–25°C reflecting typical forecast uncertainty in maximum temperature two days out. Minor shifts in the timing of frontal passage or precipitation could still nudge the observed high by 1–2°C, but current guidance supports the clustered probabilities rather than outliers above 27°C or below 22°C.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover, scattered showers, and modest southerly flow are the dominant factors keeping the highest temperature in Tokyo on August 28 near the 31–32 °C range that traders currently favor.**

Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency (issued 27 August) calls for a mostly cloudy day with occasional scattered showers, a maximum of 31–32 °C, and a minimum near 24 °C. Multiple models and international services converge on the same narrow band (31–32 °C), consistent with late-August normals of ~30–31 °C. 

Light south-to-southwest winds and high humidity limit surface heating by reducing net solar input and enhancing boundary-layer mixing. Any early-morning or midday showers further suppress the peak by cutting insolation and evaporative cooling. 

The tight clustering of market-implied probabilities across 31 °C (32.5 %), 32 °C (30 %), and 33 °C (21.5 %) reflects genuine forecast uncertainty: modest differences in cloud thickness, shower timing, or wind direction could easily shift the realized maximum by 1–2 °C. Clearer breaks or delayed rain would favor the upper end of the distribution, while persistent low-level cloud or earlier convection would cap it near 31 °C. Updated model runs and the next JMA bulletin are the key near-term catalysts that could move the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble model runs for London on August 28 point to a daytime maximum near 24 °C, with scattered afternoon showers and moderate southwesterly winds limiting surface heating. Trader consensus has narrowed between the 24 °C and 25 °C-or-higher bins because small differences in cloud cover, shower timing, and boundary-layer mixing can shift the peak by 1–2 °C. Clearer spells or delayed convection would allow brief insolation spikes toward 25 °C, while earlier or heavier showers would cap readings at 23–24 °C; historical late-August climatology (mean high ~22 °C) underscores how sensitive the outcome remains to these short-term variables ahead of tomorrow’s final observations.
